mainTopic: The size of משה's מזבח according to רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, רבא on whether the holy courtyard floor counts for blood, and רבי אלעזר's rule that offerings may not be eaten while the מזבח is damaged.
overview: First, רבי יוסי finishes explaining his view. The courtyard curtains were fifteen אמות high, and the 'five אמות' counts only from the top of the מזבח up. The 'three אמות' of the מזבח counts only from the סובב up, so the whole מזבח was ten אמות tall. Next, the גמרא defends רבי יהודה. He uses the גזירה שוה for the width, and in his view the כהן may be seen over the curtains as long as the עבודה in his hands stays hidden. Then each side explains a word in the פסוק about שלמה that seems to fit the other side: 'sanctified' and 'too small.' The root of the argument is that רבי יהודה compares outside to outside, while רבי יוסי compares a כלי to a כלי. רבא then says רבי יהודה agrees that blood needs the real מזבח, but the גמרא pushes off his proof from the ברייתא about the cup of mixed blood. Last, רבי אלעזר rules that when the מזבח is damaged, שירי מנחה and all קדשי קדשים may not be eaten. אביי begins to show the same rule for קדשים קלים from a teaching of רבי יוסי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The curtains' 'five cubits' count from the top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי continues. The curtains were fifteen אמות high, so the פסוק that says 'five אמות' must mean five above the top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...cubits to the side.' So why does the פסוק say 'five cubits'? That means from the edge of the מזבח and upward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי is still speaking. He explains two פסוקים that seem to clash about how tall the courtyard curtains were: five אמות or fifteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק gives the curtains a height of fifteen אמות, and another says 'five אמות.' רבי יוסי says fifteen is the full height from the ground. The 'five' only counts the part that stood above the top of a ten-אמה מזבח, and 10 + 5 = 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Side (literally 'shoulder'), one side of the courtyard entrance
'The פסוק teaches'; why does the פסוק say...
The top edge of the מזבח

phrases.english: cubits to the side."
phrases.notes: This finishes a פסוק that started on the last page: 'fifteen cubits to the side' (שמות 38:14).

phrases.english: And what does the verse mean by "five cubits"?
From the edge of the altar and upward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״חָמֵשׁ אַמּוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוסי's statement from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The curtains were fifteen אמות high. The 'five אמות' is measured from the top of the מזבח upward.

steps.title: The altar's 'three cubits' count from the ledge
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains that the 'three אמות' height of the מזבח counts only from the סובב upward, not from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does the פסוק say 'and its height three cubits'? That means from the edge of the סובב and upward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי deals with the פסוק that seems to make the מזבח only three אמות tall. He reads it as measuring only the top part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוסי holds the מזבח was ten אמות high, the 'three אמות' in the פסוק cannot be the full height. He says it counts from the ledge that goes around the מזבח up to the top. That way the full ten-אמה height still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The ledge that goes around the outside of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: the מזבח is ten אמות. The 'three אמות' counts from the סובב up, and the curtains' 'five אמות' counts from the top of the מזבח up.

phrases.english: And what does the verse mean by "and its height three cubits"?
From the edge of the surrounding ledge and upward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וְשָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת קוֹמָתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same explanation; this time about the מזבח's own height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'three אמות' of the מזבח is measured from the סובב upward.

steps.title: רבי יהודה uses the verbal analogy for width
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה does with רבי יוסי's גזירה שוה. He learns it, but applies it to the width of the מזבח, not its height.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? When he learns the גזירה שוה, he learns it about the width.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי יהודה, who holds the מזבח was only three אמות high. It explains what he does with the גזירה שוה that רבי יוסי used for the height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי used a גזירה שוה from the word 'square' to prove the מזבח was ten אמות tall. רבי יהודה does not reject the גזירה שוה. He just says it teaches about the width, so he can still keep the height at three.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: This is a short question: what does רבי יהודה do with the גזירה שוה that רבי יוסי used?

phrases.english: When he learns the verbal analogy,
it is about its width that he learns it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כִּי גְּמִיר גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוסי's view to defending רבי יהודה's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's three-אמה height, against רבי יוסי's גזירה שוה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the גזירה שוה to a different detail (width instead of height)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה שוה forces a ten-אמה height, and רבי יהודה has no answer to it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה uses the גזירה שוה only for the width, so the height can stay three.

steps.title: Wouldn't the priest be seen over the curtains?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: with a three-אמה מזבח and five-אמה curtains, a כהן standing on the מזבח would be visible from outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יהודה, the כהן is seen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a practical problem with רבי יהודה's view about the heights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מזבח is three אמות and the curtains are only five, a כהן standing on top of the מזבח sticks out above the curtains. People outside the courtyard would see him. That seems wrong.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda,
the priest is visible!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא קָא מִיתְחֲזֵי כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבי יהודה's view, this time from logic instead of from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that the מזבח was three אמות and the curtains five
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heights don't work: a כהן on the מזבח would stand above the curtains and be seen from outside.

steps.title: The priest is seen, but not the service in his hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה: it is fine if the כהן himself is seen, as long as the עבודה he does with his hands stays hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the כהן is seen. But the עבודה in his hand is not seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the last step and defends רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits that the כהן's head and upper body show above the curtains. What matters is that the עבודה he is doing with his hands is lower and stays hidden behind them. So רבי יהודה's measurements still work.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that... (admits a point, then limits it)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the כהן may be seen over the curtains, but the עבודה in his hands may not.

phrases.english: Granted that the priest is visible;
the service that is in his hand is not visible.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּכֹהֵן מִיתְחֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees with the fact but narrows what matters
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any part of the כהן being seen would be a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the עבודה in his hands must be hidden, and it is.

steps.title: The word 'sanctified' fits רבי יהודה, so what does רבי יוסי do with it?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says שלמה 'sanctified' the middle of the courtyard. That fits רבי יהודה, who says the floor became a מזבח. The גמרא asks what the word means for רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי יהודה, because that is why the פסוק says 'sanctified.' But for רבי יוסי, what does 'sanctified' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a word in the פסוק that seems to support רבי יהודה. It asks how רבי יוסי can explain that word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that שלמה made the courtyard floor holy so that קרבנות could be offered on it like on a מזבח. The word 'קידש' fits that perfectly. רבי יוסי does not say the floor became a מזבח, so the word seems to have no job in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one side)
That is why it is written

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
this is why it is written 'sanctified';
but according to Rabbi Yosei,
what does 'sanctified' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב קִידֵּשׁ; אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, מַאי קִידֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the original argument about the courtyard floor and checks it against the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's opinion that the courtyard floor did not become a מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses the word 'sanctified,' which seems to mean the floor became holy as a מזבח. That would be an extra word for רבי יוסי.

steps.title: For רבי יוסי, 'sanctified' means made holy to hold a מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains that שלמה sanctified the courtyard so that a מזבח could be set up there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means he sanctified it in order to set up a מזבח in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי by giving the word 'sanctified' a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard was made holy, but not as a מזבח itself. It was made holy as the proper place where a מזבח could stand. So the word 'קידש' has meaning even in רבי יוסי's view.

phrases.english: To set up a מזבח in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהַעֲמִיד בָּהּ מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Sanctified' means the floor itself became a מזבח, which only fits רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Sanctified' can mean the courtyard was made holy as a place to set up a מזבח, which fits רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The word 'too small' fits רבי יוסי, so what does רבי יהודה do with it?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the copper מזבח was 'too small.' That fits רבי יוסי, who says משה's מזבח was small. The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה explains it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי יוסי, because that is why the פסוק says 'too small.' But for רבי יהודה, what does 'too small' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא does the same thing in reverse. It points to a word in the פסוק that seems to support רבי יוסי and asks how רבי יהודה explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that משה's copper מזבח was only five by five אמות, so calling it 'too small' fits well. רבי יהודה holds it was ten by ten, which is large. So why would the פסוק call it small?

keyTerms.meaning: The copper מזבח made by משה

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yosei,
this is why it is written 'too small';
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, a little later: the copper מזבח was too small to hold all the קרבנות.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yehuda,
what does 'too small' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב קָטָן; אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַאי קָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 6. This time the challenge is against רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's opinion that משה's מזבח was ten by ten אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ten-by-ten מזבח is big, so the פסוק's word 'too small' does not seem to fit רבי יהודה.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה, 'too small' refers to שלמה's stone מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as saying that the stone מזבח שלמה built in place of the copper one was too small for all the קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: the stone מזבח that שלמה made in place of the copper מזבח was too small.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה. It changes which מזבח the word 'too small' is describing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not have to say משה's מזבח was small. The פסוק is talking about שלמה's new stone מזבח, which stood where the copper one had been. That day there were so many קרבנות that even this מזבח was not big enough, so the floor was needed too.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
the stone מזבח that שלמה made
in place of the copper מזבח
was too small.

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself says 'the copper מזבח.' רבי יהודה reads 'copper מזבח' as telling us where the stone מזבח stood, which was in place of the copper one. He does not mean the copper מזבח itself was small.
steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: מִזְבַּח אֲבָנִים שֶׁעָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה תַּחַת מִזְבַּח הַנְּחֹשֶׁת – קָטָן הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which object the פסוק describes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Too small' describes משה's copper מזבח, which fits only רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Too small' describes שלמה's stone מזבח that replaced the copper one, so it fits רבי יהודה too.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle causes רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי to disagree about the size of משה's מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is asking for the deeper reason behind the argument, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them use the word 'רבוע' (square) to learn the size of משה's מזבח. But each one compares it to a different מזבח. The גמרא wants to know why they choose different sources.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פסוקים are explained for both sides, the גמרא moves on to ask for the root of the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that makes רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי learn the גזירה שוה of 'רבוע' differently

steps.title: Outside from outside versus a vessel from a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns משה's outer מזבח from another outer מזבח (the one in יחזקאל), not from the inner one. רבי יוסי learns משה's portable מזבח from another portable כלי (the golden מזבח), not from a built structure.
steps.simpleTranslation: One חכם holds: we learn an outer מזבח from an outer מזבח, and not an outer one from an inner one. The other חכם holds: we learn a כלי from a כלי, and not a כלי from a building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing that each חכם picks the closest match for משה's מזבח, but each one has a different idea of what makes a match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה matches by location: משה's מזבח stood outside, so he compares it to יחזקאל's outer מזבח, which gives a width of ten by ten. רבי יוסי matches by type: משה's מזבח was a movable כלי, so he compares it to the golden מזבח (also a כלי), not to יחזקאל's built מזבח. Like the golden מזבח, its height is twice its width, so a five-by-five מזבח is ten אמות tall.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn / derive (one case from another)

steps.whatToRemember: Both חכמים learn from the word 'רבוע.' רבי יהודה matches by location (outside from outside). רבי יוסי matches by type of object (a כלי from a כלי). That is why they give משה's מזבח different sizes.

phrases.english: One master holds:
we learn outside from outside,
and we do not learn outside from inside;
and the other master holds:
we learn a vessel from a vessel,
and we do not learn a vessel from a building.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: דָּנִין חוּץ מִחוּץ, וְאֵין דָּנִין חוּץ מִפְּנִים; וּמָר סָבַר: דָּנִין כְּלִי מִכְּלִי, וְאֵין דָּנִין כְּלִי מִבִּנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה compares by location (outer from outer). רבי יוסי compares by type of object (a portable כלי from a portable כלי, not from a built structure).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a גזירה שוה can lead to different results depending on which similarity a חכם thinks matters most when he picks the matching case.

steps.title: רבא: רבי יהודה agrees about blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא states that רבי יהודה agrees that blood must be placed on the מזבח itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יהודה agrees regarding blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to רבי יהודה's view that the whole עזרה was sanctified. The holy floor may work for burning parts of קרבנות, but blood still needs the real מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we saw רבי יהודה say that שלמה sanctified the courtyard so it could act like a מזבח. רבא says this does not cover the blood. For blood, רבי יהודה 'agrees' with the view that only the מזבח itself counts.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees, admits (usually in one area, even though he disagrees elsewhere)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding blood.
phrases.notes: He means: even רבי יהודה agrees that blood must go on the actual מזבח, not just anywhere in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּדָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יהודה's view from step 6, that the courtyard floor was sanctified to act like a מזבח, so that it does not apply to blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the sanctified courtyard can replace the מזבח for burning, but blood must be placed on the מזבח itself.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the cup of mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says a כהן would fill a cup with the mixed blood from the floor and pour it on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יהודה says: He would fill one cup from the mixed blood and pour it on top of the altar. That way, if the blood of one of the offerings spilled, this pouring makes it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the source for his claim. It is a ברייתא about blood that mixed together on the courtyard floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lots of blood from many קרבנות mixed together on the floor. If one animal's blood had spilled completely, a bit of it would be in this cup, and pouring the cup on the מזבח would make that קרבן valid. The cup is taken up to the מזבח, so being on the holy floor was not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: mixtures, here blood of many קרבנות mixed together

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He would fill one cup
phrases.notes: This is about ערב פסח, when so much blood ended up on the courtyard floor.

phrases.english: from the mixed blood,
and pour it on top of the altar;
so that if the blood
of one of them spilled,
this turns out to make it valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבא's claim in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי יהודה requires blood to be placed on the מזבח itself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה requires pouring the mixed blood from the floor onto the מזבח.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא proves רבא's point
steps.stepSummary: If the whole עזרה counted as a מזבח for blood, the spilled blood would already be valid, so no cup would be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think רבי יהודה holds that the whole courtyard was sanctified, then its מצוה was already done!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains exactly how the ברייתא proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the floor counted like the מזבח for blood, the blood that spilled onto it would already count as placed. Then there would be no reason to scoop it up and pour it on the מזבח. Since רבי יהודה does require it, the floor must not count for blood.

keyTerms.meaning: and if it enters your mind (if you were to think)
the courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that Rabbi Yehuda holds
that the whole courtyard was sanctified,
then its מצוה was already done!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ סָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כּוּלַּהּ עֲזָרָה מִיקַּדְּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the logic of the proof brought in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that for blood, the courtyard floor does not count as the מזבח, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Pouring the cup on the מזבח would be pointless if blood on the holy floor already counted.

steps.title: Maybe the blood has to be poured by a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reason for the cup: maybe רבי יהודה requires the blood to be poured by a person, and blood that spilled by itself does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is because he holds that we need pouring done by human force?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to knock down רבא's proof by giving a different reason for the cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the floor really does count like the מזבח. The problem may be that the blood fell there by accident and no person poured it. If so, the ברייתא does not prove that the floor fails for blood.

keyTerms.meaning: but perhaps (opens a push-back against a proof)
by human force, done by a person

phrases.english: But perhaps it is because he holds
that we need pouring done by human force?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר שְׁפִיכָה מִכֹּחַ הָאָדָם בָּעֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 14 by giving another reason for the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not רבא's claim itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cup may be needed because a person has to pour the blood, not because the floor fails to count as the מזבח.

steps.title: Then just pour it back on the floor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the push-back: if the only problem were that a person must pour it, the כהן could pour the cup right back onto the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let him take it and pour it back in its place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the push-back from step 15 and so saves רבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the floor counted like the מזבח and the only thing missing was a person pouring, the כהן could pour the cup back onto the floor. The ברייתא says he pours it on the מזבח. That suggests the floor itself is not good enough for blood.

keyTerms.meaning: in its place (here: back on the floor)

phrases.english: If so, let him take it
and pour it in its place!
phrases.notes: Meaning right there on the courtyard floor, instead of carrying it up to the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נִשְׁקְלֵיהּ וְנִשְׁפֹּיךְ לֵיהּ אַדּוּכְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the push-back of step 15 and brings back רבא's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that pouring by a person explains the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Pouring by a person could be done on the floor itself, so it does not explain why the blood goes to the מזבח.

steps.title: Maybe it is just the best way to do the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again: maybe the blood is poured on the מזבח only because it is the best way to do the מצוה, even if the floor would also work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is because we want the מצוה done in the best possible way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason why the ברייתא does not prove רבא's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the floor counts like the מזבח for blood, putting the blood on the real מזבח is the best way to do it. That alone could explain why the כהן carries the cup up. So the ברייתא no longer proves that the floor fails for blood.

keyTerms.meaning: doing a מצוה in the best, most ideal way

steps.whatToRemember: רבא tried to prove that רבי יהודה requires blood on the real מזבח. The גמרא's last word here is that the ברייתא may only show the best way to do the מצוה, so the proof is pushed off.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say רבא is wrong. It only says this ברייתא is not a proof for him.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is because
we want the מצוה done in the best way?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּבָעֵינַן מִצְוָה מִן הַמּוּבְחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 16 saved the proof, this gives a new reason that weakens it again.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's proof from the ברייתא, but does not show that his claim is false.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Pouring on the מזבח may just be the best way to do the מצוה, not a requirement, so the floor could still count after the fact.

steps.title: A damaged altar stops the eating of the leftover meal offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that if the מזבח is damaged, the כהנים may not eat שירי מנחה. He learns it from the words 'beside the altar' in ויקרא 10:12.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: if the מזבח got damaged, you may not eat the leftover part of a מנחה because of it. The פסוק says, 'Eat it as מצות beside the altar.' But did they really have to eat it right next to the מזבח? No. The פסוק must mean: eat it only when the מזבח is whole, and not when it is missing a piece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבי אלעזר gives a rule about a damaged מזבח and shows where he learns it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'beside the altar' cannot be telling us where to eat, because the מנחה did not have to be eaten right next to the מזבח. So רבי אלעזר reads them differently: the eating depends on the מזבח being there and whole. If the מזבח is damaged, the leftovers may not be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: An altar that was damaged, with a piece broken off
The leftover part of a meal offering, which the כהנים eat
Because of it, on its account
But is it really so? It opens a question showing that the plain reading can't be right

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: when the מזבח is damaged, שירי מנחה may not be eaten. The source is 'beside the altar', read as 'while the altar is whole.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
An altar that was damaged:
one may not eat, on its account, the remainder of a meal offering,
as it is stated: "And eat it as matzos beside the altar"
But did they eat it beside the altar?!
Rather, it means at a time when it is whole,
and not at a time when it is lacking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אלעזר מזבח שנפגם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the argument about רבי יהודה and the spilled blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the מזבח is damaged, שירי מנחה may not be eaten. This is learned from 'beside the altar', read as 'while the altar is whole.'

steps.title: What about the other most-holy offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the source so far covers only שירי מנחה. It asks how we know the same rule for all קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for the leftover מנחה. How do we know the rule for all the most-holy offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי אלעזר's rule reaches past the מנחה. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק רבי אלעזר used is about a מנחה. So the גמרא needs a separate source to apply the rule to other קדשי קדשים, such as a חטאת or an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for this case)
Offerings of the most holy level
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found a source for the remainder of a meal offering;
offerings of the most sacred order, from where do we derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אשכחן שירי מנחה קדשי קדשים מנלן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the rule from step 18 also covers other offerings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that applies the damaged-מזבח rule to all קדשי קדשים.

steps.title: The words 'most holy' bring in all most-holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the words 'קדש קדשים' in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'it is most holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 19 by pointing to the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the מנחה 'קדש קדשים', which is the name used for all the most-holy offerings. That name links them, so the damaged-מזבח rule applies to all of them, not only to the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Most holy, the words in the פסוק
And eat it, the start of the פסוק being explained

phrases.english: The verse states: "most holy."
phrases.notes: These words are at the end of the same פסוק, ויקרא 10:12.

steps.triggerLanguage: תלמוד לומר קדש קדשים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'קדש קדשים' in the פסוק extend the rule to all קדשי קדשים.

steps.title: What about offerings of lesser holiness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the damaged-מזבח rule for קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the rule for offerings of lesser holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes one level further and asks about the less-holy offerings. It is setting up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'קדש קדשים' only cover the most-holy offerings. קדשים קלים are not called by that name, so they need their own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Light, meaning a lower level of holiness

phrases.english: Offerings of lesser sanctity, from where do we derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: קדשים קלים מנין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 20 and asks about the next group of offerings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that applies the damaged-מזבח rule to קדשים קלים.

steps.title: אביי learns it from a teaching of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the rule for קדשים קלים comes from a teaching of רבי יוסי, and starts to quote a ברייתא where רבי יוסי says three things in someone's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it comes from a teaching of רבי יוסי, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says three things in the name of...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to answer the question about קדשים קלים by bringing a ברייתא of רבי יוסי. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not use a new פסוק. He points to a teaching that רבי יוסי already gave. We will only see how it proves the rule once the rest of the ברייתא is quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from (it is learned from)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is derived from the exposition of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מִשּׁוּם
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says three matters in the name of

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי אתיא מדרשא דרבי יוסי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule for קדשים קלים is learned from a teaching of רבי יוסי, quoted in a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.
